questions.question:
A train starts from rest and reaches a velocity of 36 km/hr in 3 minutes with uniform acceleration.

What is the distance covered by the train during this time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**900 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The train starts from **rest**, which means the **initial velocity (u)** is **0 m/s**. When an object begins its motion from a stationary position, its starting speed is always considered zero in kinematic calculations.
 
• The **final velocity (v)** given is **36 km/hr**. To perform calculations in **SI units**, this must be converted to **meters per second (m/s)**. By multiplying **36** by the conversion factor **5/18**, we get **10 m/s**.
 
• The **time (t)** taken to reach this velocity is **3 minutes**. In physics equations, time must be expressed in **seconds**. Therefore, **3 minutes** is multiplied by **60**, resulting in **180 seconds**.
 
• Since the train moves with **uniform acceleration (a)**, we can find the acceleration using the first equation of motion: **v = u + at**. Substituting the values, **10 = 0 + a(180)**, which gives **a = 10/180** or **1/18 m/s²**.
 
• The **distance (s)** covered is calculated using the second equation of motion: **s = ut + (1/2)at²**. Substituting the known values: **s = (0)(180) + (1/2)(1/18)(180)(180)**. This simplifies to **s = 0 + (1/2)(1/18)(32400)**, which equals **900 meters**.
 
• Alternatively, distance can be found using **average velocity** multiplied by **time** for uniform acceleration: **[(u + v) / 2] x t**. Here, **[(0 + 10) / 2] x 180 = 5 x 180 = 900 m**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 900 m.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Equations of Motion:**
 
 
• These equations describe the behavior of a physical system in terms of its motion as a function of time. There are three primary equations for **uniform acceleration**: **v = u + at**, **s = ut + 1/2 at²**, and **v² = u² + 2as**.
 
• These were derived based on the work of **Sir Isaac Newton** and describe linear motion. They are only applicable when **acceleration** remains **constant** throughout the duration of the motion.
 
 
 
• **Unit Conversion Logic:**
 
 
• Converting **km/hr** to **m/s** is a standard procedure in physics. Since **1 kilometer** is **1000 meters** and **1 hour** is **3600 seconds**, the ratio **1000/3600** simplifies to **5/18**.
 
• This conversion is essential to maintain consistency with the **International System of Units (SI)**, where distance is in **meters** and time is in **seconds**.
 
 
 
• **Uniform Acceleration:**
 
 
• **Uniform acceleration** occurs when the **velocity** of an object changes by an **equal amount** in every **equal time interval**.
 
• On a **Velocity-Time (v-t) graph**, uniform acceleration is represented by a **straight line**. The **area under the line** in a v-t graph represents the **total distance** covered by the object.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scalar vs Vector:** **Distance** is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it only has magnitude. However, in straight-line motion in a single direction starting from rest, the magnitude of **distance** and **displacement** (a vector) are identical.
 
• **Significance of "Rest":** In competitive exams, the phrase "starts from rest" is a crucial **data point** indicating that **u = 0**. Conversely, "comes to a stop" or "brakes are applied" usually indicates **v = 0**.
 
• **Numerical Accuracy:** Always ensure all units are converted to the **MKS system** (Meter-Kilogram-Second) before applying kinematic formulas to avoid common calculation errors. For this problem, failing to convert **3 minutes** to **180 seconds** would lead to an incorrect result.

questions.question: In plants, how does sexual reproduction leads to better survival in offspring?

options.text: Offspring do not show any variation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Offspring show new genetic recombination**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sexual reproduction** in plants involves the fusion of male and female **gametes** to form a **zygote**, which eventually develops into a new individual.
 
• One of the most significant features of this process is **genetic recombination**. During the process of **meiosis** (cell division to produce gametes), **crossing over** occurs between **homologous chromosomes** during **prophase I**. This results in offspring having a unique combination of genes different from both parents. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• This **genetic variation** is the cornerstone of **survival** in changing environments. It allows a population of plants to adapt to new **pathogens**, changing **climatic conditions**, and **competition** for resources.
 
• In contrast, if offspring do not show any variation, they are highly susceptible to being wiped out by a single disease or environmental change. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Offspring produced through sexual reproduction are not **clones**; they are genetically distinct individuals. **Cloning** is a characteristic of **asexual reproduction** or **vegetative propagation**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Sexual reproduction** is generally a slower process compared to asexual reproduction because it involves complex stages like **pollination**, **fertilization**, **seed formation**, and **dormancy**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mechanism of Variation:** The two main sources of variation in sexual reproduction are **independent assortment** of chromosomes and **crossing over**. In **angiosperms** (flowering plants), the **pollen grain** (male gametophyte) and **embryo sac** (female gametophyte) undergo these processes to ensure diversity.
 
• **Evolutionary Advantage:** **Variation** is the raw material for **natural selection**. Plants with favorable genetic traits resulting from recombination are more likely to survive and reproduce, passing those advantageous traits to the next generation.
 
• **Types of Pollination:** **Cross-pollination** (Allogamy) specifically promotes greater **heterozygosity** and **genetic diversity** compared to **self-pollination** (Autogamy).
 
• **Adaptability:** Recombination allows for the masking of **harmful mutations**. Since offspring receive sets of genes from two parents, a healthy gene from one parent can often compensate for a defective gene from the other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Asexual Reproduction:** In **asexual reproduction**, such as **budding**, **fragmentation**, or **apomixis**, the offspring are **genetically identical** to the parent. While this allows for rapid population growth in stable environments, it lacks the **evolutionary flexibility** provided by sexual reproduction.
 
• **Environmental Stress:** In unpredictable environments (e.g., fluctuating **soil pH**, **drought**, or **salinity**), the **recombinant genotypes** produced through sexual reproduction have a higher probability of possessing the necessary physiological traits to withstand **abiotic stress**.
 
• **Date and Discovery:** The basic principles of heredity and the importance of variation were famously documented by **Gregor Mendel** in the **mid-19th century** (around **1865**) through his experiments on **Pisum sativum** (pea plants).
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is true regarding the twinkling of the stars? 
(i) The stars twinkle as they have light of their own. 
(ii) The stars twinkle due to reflection of light. 
(iii) There is apparent change in the position of the star during the night time. 
(iv) The stars twinkle due to atmospheric refraction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (iii) and (iv)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atmospheric Refraction** is the primary physical phenomenon responsible for the twinkling of stars. As starlight enters the Earth's **atmosphere**, it undergoes **refraction** continuously before it reaches the **Earth's surface**. ***Hence, statement (iv) is correct.***
 
• The **apparent position** of a star is slightly different from its **actual position** because the atmosphere bends starlight toward the **normal** as it moves from a **rarer medium** to an **optically denser medium**. Because the physical conditions of the Earth's atmosphere are not stationary, the **apparent position** of the star fluctuates slightly. ***Hence, statement (iii) is correct.***
 
• While it is scientifically true that stars are **self-luminous** bodies (they have light of their own), this characteristic is not the cause of the **twinkling effect**. Twinkling is an **optical illusion** created by the medium through which the light travels, not the source of the light itself. ***Hence, statement (i) is a true fact but not the reason for twinkling.***
 
• The twinkling of stars is caused by the **refraction** (bending) of light, not the **reflection** of light. **Reflection** involves light bouncing off a surface, whereas **refraction** involves light passing through a medium of varying **optical density**. ***Hence, statement (ii) is incorrect.***
 
• The path of rays of light coming from the star goes on varying slightly, the **apparent position** of the star fluctuates and the amount of starlight entering the eye **flickers**—the star sometimes appears brighter, and at some other time, fainter, which is the **twinkling effect**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Point Source vs. Extended Source**:
 
 
• Stars are located at a **vast distance** from the Earth, often measured in **light-years**. This makes them appear as **point-sized sources** of light. Even a tiny **atmospheric disturbance** can significantly shift the path of a single point of light.
 
• In contrast, **planets** are much closer to Earth and are seen as **extended sources** or a collection of many point-sized sources of light. The total variation in the amount of light entering our eye from all the individual point-sized sources will **average out to zero**, which is why **planets do not twinkle**.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index of Air**:
 
 
• The Earth's atmosphere consists of several layers with varying **temperatures** and **densities**. Cold air is **optically denser** than warm air, meaning it has a higher **refractive index**.
 
• As starlight passes through these turbulent layers, the light is constantly **bent** back and forth. This process is known as **stellar scintillation**.
 
 
 
• **Position Near Horizon**:
 
 
• Stars appear to twinkle more when they are near the **horizon** compared to when they are directly overhead (at the **zenith**). This is because the light must travel through a **thicker layer** of the atmosphere, encountering more **turbulence** and **refraction**.
 
 
 
• **Vacuum of Space**:
 
 
• If an observer were in **outer space** (a **vacuum**), stars would not twinkle. This is why **space telescopes** like the **Hubble Space Telescope** or **James Webb Space Telescope** can capture much clearer images than ground-based telescopes, as they are above the **distorting effects** of the Earth's atmosphere.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **speed of light** changes as it moves through different **optical media**, causing the bending effect known as **refraction**.
 
• The **Laws of Refraction** (Snell's Law) dictate that when light travels from a **vacuum** into the atmosphere, it slows down and bends toward the **normal**.
 
• The **apparent shift** in position means a star always appears **slightly higher** in the sky than its **actual position**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic property of ionic compounds?

options.text: Poor electrical conductivity in molten state

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Strong electrostatic forces between ions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ionic compounds** are chemical compounds composed of **ions** held together by **electrostatic forces** termed **ionic bonding**. These compounds are formed through the **transfer of electrons** from a **metal** to a **non-metal**.
 
• The most defining characteristic of these compounds is the existence of **strong electrostatic forces of attraction** between the oppositely charged **cations** (positively charged) and **anions** (negatively charged). ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Because of these **strong inter-ionic attractions**, ionic compounds exist as **solids** and are generally **hard**. A significant amount of **thermal energy** is required to overcome these forces, which results in **high melting and boiling points**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Ionic compounds are generally **soluble in polar solvents** like **water** because the water molecules reduce the electrostatic attraction between the ions, allowing them to disperse. However, they are usually **insoluble** in **non-polar solvents** such as **benzene**, **ether**, or **kerosene**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• In their **solid state**, ionic compounds are **poor conductors** of electricity because the ions are fixed in a **crystal lattice**. However, in the **molten state** or when dissolved in **aqueous solution**, the ions become free to move and act as **charge carriers**, making them **good electrical conductors**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Formation of Ionic Bonds:**
 
 
• An **ionic bond** is formed when one atom (typically a metal) loses **valence electrons** to another atom (typically a non-metal). For example, in **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, a **sodium atom** loses one electron to become **Na+**, and a **chlorine atom** gains that electron to become **Cl-**.
 
• The resulting **electrostatic attraction** between the **sodium cation** and **chloride anion** creates the stable compound.
 
 
 
• **Crystal Lattice Structure:**
 
 
• Ionic compounds do not exist as single molecules; instead, they form a **three-dimensional network** called a **crystal lattice**.
 
• This **lattice structure** is highly organized and contributes to the **brittleness** of the compound, as applying pressure shifts the ions and causes like-charged ions to repel each other, shattering the crystal.
 
 
 
• **Lattice Energy:**
 
 
• **Lattice energy** is the amount of **energy released** when **gaseous ions** combine to form one mole of an ionic solid. It is a measure of the **stability** and **strength** of the ionic bond.
 
• Higher **charge density** on ions and smaller **ionic radii** generally lead to higher lattice energy and higher **melting points**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Physical State:** At **room temperature**, almost all ionic compounds are **crystalline solids** due to the high **bond strength**.
 
• **Non-directional Nature:** Unlike **covalent bonds**, ionic bonds are **non-directional** because the electrostatic field of an ion acts in all directions around it.
 
• **Applications:** Common examples include **Magnesium Oxide (MgO)**, used as a refractory material due to its extremely high melting point of **2,852 degrees Celsius**, and **Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3)**, found in **limestone** and **shells**.
 
• **Electrolysis:** The **molten state** conductivity of ionic compounds is utilized in **industrial electrolysis** to extract reactive metals like **Aluminum** and **Sodium** from their ores.
</ul

questions.question: The velocity-time graph of a particle moving with uniform acceleration is a:

options.text: straight line inclined to time axis

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**straight line inclined to time axis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uniform acceleration** is defined as a type of motion where the **velocity** of an object changes by an **equal amount** in every **equal time interval**. In other words, the rate of change of velocity remains **constant** over **time**.
 
• On a **velocity-time (v-t) graph**, the **slope** of the line represents the **acceleration** of the particle. If the **acceleration** is **uniform** (constant), the **slope** must also be **constant**.
 
• A **straight line** is the geometric representation of a **constant slope**. Therefore, the graph of an object moving with **uniform acceleration** is a **straight line**.
 
• The line must be **inclined to the time axis** (x-axis) to show that **velocity** is changing. If the acceleration is **positive**, the line slopes **upward**; if the acceleration is **negative** (retardation), the line slopes **downward**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• A **horizontal line** on a **velocity-time graph** indicates that the **slope is zero**, meaning the **acceleration** is **0** and the particle is moving with **uniform velocity**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• A **curve concave upward** indicates that the **slope** (acceleration) is **increasing** over **time**, which represents **non-uniform acceleration**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• A **vertical line** would imply that **velocity** changes **infinitely** at a single **point in time**, resulting in **infinite acceleration**, which is physically impossible for a particle. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Area under the Graph:** The **area** enclosed by the **velocity-time graph** and the **time axis** represents the **total displacement** of the particle during that **time interval**.
 
• **Equations of Motion:** For a particle moving with **uniform acceleration (a)**, the relationship between **initial velocity (u)**, **final velocity (v)**, and **time (t)** is given by the equation **v = u + at**. This is a **linear equation** of the form y = mx + c, confirming that the graph is a **straight line**.
 
• **Slope Calculation:** The **slope** of the **velocity-time graph** is calculated as the **change in velocity** divided by the **change in time** (rise over run). For **uniform acceleration**, this ratio is always the same regardless of which two points on the line are chosen.
 
• **Types of V-T Graphs:**
 
 
• **Zero Acceleration:** A **straight line parallel** to the **time axis**.
 
• **Positive Uniform Acceleration:** A **straight line** with a **positive slope** starting from the **origin** (if u=0) or from the **y-axis** (if u>0).
 
• **Negative Uniform Acceleration:** A **straight line** with a **negative slope** (moving towards the time axis).
 
• **Non-Uniform Acceleration:** Any **curved line** (parabolic, exponential, etc.).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Position-Time Graph:** For a particle with **uniform acceleration**, the **position-time (s-t) graph** is a **parabola**, because **displacement** is proportional to the **square of time** (s = ut + 1/2 at²).
 
• **Instantaneous Acceleration:** In cases of **non-uniform acceleration**, the **acceleration** at a specific **moment** is found by drawing a **tangent** to the **velocity-time curve** at that **point** and finding its **slope**.
 
• **Units:** The **SI unit** of **acceleration** is **meters per second squared (m/s²)**, while **velocity** is measured in **meters per second (m/s)**.
 
• **Kinematics:** These graphical interpretations are fundamental in **Kinematics**, a branch of **Physics** that describes the **motion** of points, bodies, and systems without considering the **forces** that cause the motion.
</ul

questions.question: In stethoscopes, the sound of the heartbeat is transmitted to the doctor’s ears because:

options.text: the sound waves are absorbed by the tube walls
the sound waves undergo successive refraction in the tube
the sound waves are amplified by electricity
the sound waves are guided by multiple reflections in the tube

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the sound waves are guided by multiple reflections in the tube**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **stethoscope** is a **medical instrument** used by doctors for listening to sounds produced within the body, chiefly in the **heart** or **lungs**.
 
• In stethoscopes, the sound of the patient’s heartbeat reaches the doctor’s ears by **multiple reflection** of sound waves. The sound travels through the **hollow tube** of the stethoscope by reflecting off its inner walls repeatedly until it reaches the **earpieces**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The **sound waves** are not absorbed by the tube walls; instead, the walls are designed to be reflective to ensure the **intensity** of the sound is maintained over the distance of the tube. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Refraction** involves the bending of waves when passing from one medium to another. In a stethoscope, the primary mechanism for guiding sound through the curved tube is reflection, not refraction. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• While **electronic stethoscopes** exist today that can amplify sound using **electricity**, the standard acoustic stethoscope works purely on the principle of **acoustics** and **physical reflection** without any electrical amplification. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Invention:** The stethoscope was invented in **France** in **1816** by **René Laennec**. Originally, it was a simple **wooden tube** used for **auscultation** (listening to internal sounds).
 
• **Mechanism of Sound:** Sound is a **longitudinal mechanical wave** that requires a **medium** (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel. It travels through the stethoscope tube as a series of **compressions** and **rarefactions**.
 
• **Multiple Reflection:** This phenomenon occurs when a wave hits a surface and bounces back. By using a **closed tube**, the sound energy is confined, preventing the sound from spreading in all directions (**spherical divergence**), which effectively **amplifies** the sound heard by the doctor.
 
• **Components:** A modern stethoscope consists of a **chest piece** (which usually has a **diaphragm** and a **bell**), **tubing**, and **earpieces**. The **diaphragm** is used for **high-frequency** sounds, while the **bell** is used for **low-frequency** sounds.
 
• **Acoustic Impedance:** The design of the stethoscope helps in matching the **acoustic impedance** between the air and the body, allowing more sound energy to be transmitted to the doctor's ears.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reflection Law:** Sound follows the same **laws of reflection** as light, where the **angle of incidence** is equal to the **angle of reflection**.
 
• **Application:** Apart from stethoscopes, the principle of **multiple reflection** is also used in **megaphones**, **horns**, and **musical instruments** like **trumpets** and **shehnais** to direct sound in a specific direction.
 
• **Concert Halls:** The **ceilings** of **cinema halls** and **concert halls** are often **curved** so that sound, after reflection, reaches all corners of the hall uniformly.
 
• **Sound Absorption:** Soft materials like **curtains** or **carpets** are used in rooms to **absorb sound** and prevent **reverberation**, which is the opposite of what is required inside a stethoscope tube.

questions.question: Adding dilute hydrochloric acid to zinc granules produces hydrogen gas. This is an example of which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chemical change**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Chemical change** is a process where one or more substances are altered into one or more **new and different substances**. In the given reaction, **Zinc granules** react with **dilute Hydrochloric acid** to produce **Zinc chloride** and **Hydrogen gas**.
 
• This reaction is characterized by the **evolution of a gas**, which is one of the primary indicators of a chemical transformation. The formation of **Hydrogen bubbles** (effervescence) around the zinc metal signifies that the original identity of the reactants has changed.
 
• Unlike a physical change, this process involves the **breaking and forming of chemical bonds**. The **Zinc (Zn)** atoms displace the **Hydrogen (H)** atoms from the **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)**, resulting in a completely new chemical arrangement.
 
• Chemical changes are typically **irreversible** by simple physical methods like filtration or evaporation. Once the **Zinc chloride** salt is formed in the solution and **Hydrogen gas** is released into the atmosphere, the original **Zinc** metal cannot be recovered by mere physical cooling or mixing.
 
• The reaction is also **exothermic** in nature, meaning it is accompanied by the **release of heat**, causing the temperature of the reaction vessel to rise. This change in energy is another hallmark of a **Chemical change**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

questions.question: What happens to the energy of an object just before it hits the ground while falling freely?

options.text: Its potential energy is at its highest, and its kinetic energy becomes lowest.
It has equal amounts of potential and kinetic energy.
Its kinetic energy becomes highest, and its potential energy becomes lowest.
Both its kinetic and potential energy become zero.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Its kinetic energy becomes highest, and its potential energy becomes lowest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Law of Conservation of Energy**, energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another. In a **free-falling object**, the total **mechanical energy** (the sum of potential and kinetic energy) remains **constant** at every point of its motion.
 
• **Potential Energy (PE)** is the energy possessed by an object due to its position or **height**. It is calculated by the formula **PE = mgh**, where **m** is **mass**, **g** is **acceleration due to gravity**, and **h** is **height**. As the object falls, its **height** decreases, causing its **potential energy** to decrease continuously. Just before hitting the ground, the height is approximately **zero**, making the potential energy **lowest**.
 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE)** is the energy possessed by an object due to its **motion**. It is calculated by the formula **KE = 1/2 mv²**, where **v** is **velocity**. During a free fall, the object accelerates downward due to **gravity** at a rate of approximately **9.8 m/s²**. This constant acceleration increases the **velocity** of the object, reaching its **maximum value** just before impact. Therefore, its **kinetic energy** becomes **highest** at this point.
 
• As the object falls, there is a continuous **transformation** of **gravitational potential energy** into **kinetic energy**. At the highest point (before release), the energy is entirely potential; just before hitting the ground, it is almost entirely kinetic. ***Hence, the statement that kinetic energy is highest and potential energy is lowest is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mechanical Energy:** This refers to the sum of **Kinetic Energy** and **Potential Energy**. In the absence of air resistance, the **total mechanical energy** of a system is **conserved**. For a falling body, **Total Energy = mgh + 1/2 mv²**.
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):** On **Earth**, this value is approximately **9.8 m/s²**. It means that for every **second** an object falls, its **velocity** increases by **9.8 meters per second**. This acceleration is independent of the **mass** of the object in a vacuum.
 
• **Free Fall:** A state of motion where the only force acting upon an object is **gravity**. In real-world scenarios, **air resistance** (drag) eventually balances the force of gravity, leading to a constant speed known as **terminal velocity**, but in basic physics problems, air resistance is usually neglected.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem:** This theorem states that the **work done** by all forces acting on a particle equals the change in its **kinetic energy**. In this case, the work done by **gravity** as the object descends increases its kinetic energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• At the **maximum height**, the **velocity** of the object is **zero**, which means the **kinetic energy** is **zero** and **potential energy** is at its **maximum**.
 
• At the **mid-point** of the fall, the **potential energy** lost is exactly equal to the **kinetic energy** gained (assuming it started from rest), meaning **PE equals KE** at this specific height.
 
• Immediately **after** hitting the ground, the **kinetic energy** is transformed into other forms of energy such as **heat energy**, **sound energy**, and **potential energy of deformation**, following the principle of **energy conservation**.
 
• The **mass** of the object does not affect the **final velocity** just before hitting the ground in a vacuum, as seen in the equation **v = √(2gh)**, where mass **m** cancels out.

Select the correct option regarding the following two statements labelled Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Zinc can displace copper from copper sulphate solution.
Reason (R): Zinc is less reactive than copper.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A)** states that **Zinc** can displace **copper** from a **copper sulphate** solution. This occurs because **Zinc** is a more chemically active metal than copper, allowing it to substitute the copper ions in the solution. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• **Reason (R)** claims that **Zinc** is less reactive than **copper**. In the **electrochemical series** or **reactivity series**, **Zinc** is positioned well above **copper**, indicating it has a higher tendency to lose electrons and form cations. ***Hence, statement R is incorrect.***
 
• The chemical reaction for this process is: **Zn (solid) + CuSO4 (aqueous) → ZnSO4 (aqueous) + Cu (solid)**.
 
• During this reaction, the **blue color** of the **copper sulphate** solution gradually fades and eventually becomes **colorless** as **zinc sulphate** is formed, while **reddish-brown copper** metal deposits on the **zinc** strip.
 
• Since the **Assertion** is a factually correct chemical observation and the **Reason** is a factually incorrect statement regarding metal activity, the correct choice is that **A is true but R is false**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reactivity Series:** It is an arrangement of metals in the descending order of their **reactivities**. Metals like **Potassium (K)** and **Sodium (Na)** are at the top, while noble metals like **Gold (Au)** and **Platinum (Pt)** are at the bottom. **Zinc (Zn)** has an **atomic number** of **30** and is more reactive than **Hydrogen**, whereas **Copper (Cu)** with **atomic number 29** is less reactive than **Hydrogen**.
 
• **Displacement Reaction:** This is a type of reaction where a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound. This can be categorized into **single displacement** (like the **Zn-CuSO4** reaction) and **double displacement** reactions.
 
• **Zinc (Zn):** It is a **transition metal** found in **Group 12** of the periodic table. It is widely used in **galvanization** to prevent the **rusting** of iron because it is more reactive and oxidizes preferentially.
 
• **Copper (Cu):** It is a **transition metal** in **Group 11**. It is known for its high **electrical conductivity** and **ductility**. In nature, it often exists as **sulfide ores** like **chalcopyrite**.
 
• **Copper Sulphate (CuSO4):** Often referred to as **blue vitriol**, this salt is commonly used as a **fungicide** and in **electroplating**. Its pentahydrate form is characteristically **bright blue**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Redox Reaction:** The displacement of copper by zinc is also a **redox** (reduction-oxidation) reaction. **Zinc** undergoes **oxidation** (loses electrons to become **Zn2+**), and **Copper** ions undergo **reduction** (gain electrons to become **Cu** metal).
 
• **Practical Application:** This principle is utilized in **Voltaic cells** or **Daniel cells**, where the difference in **electrode potential** between **Zinc** and **Copper** is used to generate **electricity**.
 
• **Observation in Laboratory:** If a **copper** wire is placed in a **zinc sulphate** solution, **no reaction** occurs because **copper** cannot displace **zinc** due to its lower reactivity.
 
• **Valency:** In this reaction, both **Zinc** and **Copper** typically exhibit a **valency** of **+2**.

__
 
• **Biological magnification**, also known as biomagnification, refers to the **increase in the concentration** of a substance, such as a toxic chemical or **pesticide**, in the tissues of organisms at successively higher levels in a **food chain**.
 
• When crops like **wheat, rice, vegetables**, and **fruits** are grown, farmers often use **pesticides** and fertilizers to protect them from pests and diseases. These chemicals are absorbed by the plants from the soil or water.
 
• Because these substances are often **non-biodegradable**, they cannot be broken down by the metabolic processes of the organism nor excreted efficiently. *Hence, the presence of residues in food items is primarily due to biological magnification.*
 
• As we move up the **trophic levels**, from producers (plants) to primary consumers (herbivores) and then to secondary or tertiary consumers (like humans eating **meat**), the concentration of these harmful chemicals increases.
 
• Human beings occupy the **topmost level** in many food chains; therefore, the maximum concentration of these toxic chemicals gets accumulated in our bodies. This is why food items, especially animal products, often contain higher **pesticide residues** than the plants themselves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Transpiration:**
 
 
• It is the biological process by which **water vapor** is lost from the aerial parts of a plant, primarily through the **stomata** in leaves.
 
• This process helps in the **transportation of minerals** from the soil to various parts of the plant and aids in temperature regulation (cooling the plant). It does not involve the accumulation of toxic residues.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• This is the process by which **green plants** and some other organisms use **sunlight** to synthesize foods with the help of **chlorophyll**, carbon dioxide, and water.
 
• The primary function is the production of **glucose** and oxygen. While it is the basis of the food chain, it is a metabolic process for energy production and not for toxin accumulation.
 
 
 
• **Eutrophication:**
 
 
• This phenomenon occurs when a **water body** becomes overly enriched with nutrients (like **nitrogen** and **phosphorus**), frequently due to **agricultural runoff**.
 
• This leads to the excessive growth of **algae** (algal blooms), which depletes the **dissolved oxygen** in the water, causing the death of aquatic animals like fish. This affects water ecosystems rather than the direct residue buildup in land-based food crops.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **DDT (Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane):** One of the most famous examples of biological magnification involves the pesticide **DDT**. It was widely used in the **mid-20th century** and led to the thinning of eggshells in **predatory birds** (like eagles) because the concentration of DDT increased significantly as it moved up the food chain.
 
• **Bioaccumulation vs. Biomagnification:** **Bioaccumulation** occurs within a **single organism** over its lifetime, where the rate of intake of a substance is higher than the rate of excretion. **Biomagnification** is the cumulative result of bioaccumulation occurring across **multiple trophic levels**.
 
• **Health Impacts:** High levels of **pesticide residues** in human food can lead to long-term health issues, including **hormonal imbalances**, reproductive issues, **cancer**, and damage to the **nervous system**.
 
• **Heavy Metals:** Besides pesticides, heavy metals like **mercury**, **lead**, and **cadmium** are also subject to biological magnification, often entering the food chain through industrial waste and contaminated water.
</ul

questions.question: If the radius of the Earth is halved and the masses of both interacting objects are tripled, while keeping the distance between them unchanged, how will the gravitational force between them change?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increases 9 times**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**, the force of attraction between two objects is **directly proportional** to the product of their **masses** and **inversely proportional** to the **square of the distance** between their centers.
 
• The mathematical formula for gravitational force is **F = G (m1 * m2) / r²**, where **G** is the **Universal Gravitational Constant**, **m1** and **m2** are the **masses** of the two objects, and **r** is the **distance** between them.
 
• In this scenario, the **masses** of both interacting objects (e.g., the **Earth** and another object) are **tripled**. This means the new masses are **3m1** and **3m2**.
 
• The problem specifies that the **distance (r)** between the objects remains **unchanged**. Although the **radius of the Earth** is stated to be **halved**, this is a **distractor** because the **center-to-center distance** is explicitly held **constant**.
 
• Substituting the new values into the formula: **F' = G (3m1 * 3m2) / r²**. This simplifies to **F' = 9 * [G (m1 * m2) / r²]**, which is **9 times** the **original force (F)**. ***Hence, the gravitational force increases 9 times.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G):** It was first measured experimentally by **Henry Cavendish** in **1798**. Its accepted value is approximately **6.674 x 10^-11 N m²/kg²**.
 
• **Inverse Square Law:** This principle implies that if the **distance** between two objects is **doubled**, the **gravitational force** becomes **one-fourth (1/4)** of its original strength. If the distance is **halved**, the force **increases 4 times**.
 
• **Mass vs. Weight:** **Mass** is an **intrinsic property** of matter and remains constant regardless of **location**, while **weight** is the **gravitational force** acting on that mass and changes based on the local **acceleration due to gravity (g)**.
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):** On the **surface of the Earth**, the value of **g** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**. It is calculated using the formula **g = GM / R²**, where **M** is the **mass of the Earth** and **R** is its **radius**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vector Nature:** **Gravitational force** is always **attractive** and acts along the line joining the **centers of mass** of the two interacting bodies.
 
• **Weak Force:** Among the **four fundamental forces** of nature (Gravitational, Electromagnetic, Strong Nuclear, and Weak Nuclear), **gravity** is the **weakest**, yet it dominates on **astronomical scales**.
 
• **Range:** The **range** of gravitational force is **infinite**, meaning every object in the **universe** exerts a gravitational pull on every other object, no matter how **far** apart they are.
 
• **History:** **Sir Isaac Newton** published this law in his work **"Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica"** in **July 1687**, providing a unified explanation for both **terrestrial gravity** and **planetary motion**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included among the four Labour Codes implemented in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Code on Education, 2021**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Government of India has consolidated **29 Central Labour Laws** into **four comprehensive Labour Codes** to simplify and modernize the legal framework for the workforce.
 
• The four codes are: the **Code on Wages, 2019**; the **Industrial Relations Code, 2020**; the **Code on Social Security, 2020**; and the **Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020**.
 
• **Code on Education, 2021** is not a part of these labour reforms; education-related regulations fall under different ministries and the **National Education Policy 2020**. ***Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.***
 
• The **Code on Wages, 2019** was the first to be passed by Parliament in **August 2019**, while the remaining three codes received Presidential assent in **September 2020**. ***Hence, statement 1, 3, and 4 are included in the codes.***
 
• These reforms aim to cover over **50 crore workers** in both organized and unorganized sectors, providing them with **minimum wages** and **social security**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Code on Wages, 2019:**
 
 
• This code replaces **four laws**: the **Minimum Wages Act, 1948**, the **Payment of Wages Act, 1936**, the **Payment of Bonus Act, 1965**, and the **Equal Remuneration Act, 1976**.
 
• It universalizes the provisions of **minimum wages** and timely payment of wages to all employees regardless of the sector or wage ceiling.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Relations Code, 2020:**
 
 
• It amalgamates the **Trade Unions Act, 1926**, the **Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946**, and the **Industrial Disputes Act, 1947**.
 
• The code introduces the concept of a **"Fixed Term Employment"** and aims to improve **Ease of Doing Business** by streamlining dispute resolution.
 
 
 
• **Code on Social Security, 2020:**
 
 
• This code subsumes **nine central labour laws** including the **Employees’ Provident Fund Act** and the **Maternity Benefit Act**.
 
• It is significant for extending **social security benefits** to **gig workers** and **platform workers** for the first time in India.
 
 
 
• **Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020:**
 
 
• It merges **13 central labour laws** regulating the health and safety of workers in **factories**, **mines**, and **plantations**.
 
• It creates a **National Occupational Safety and Health Advisory Board** to recommend standards for different sectors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The implementation of these codes has been a major focus of the **Ministry of Labour and Employment**, with a transition target set towards **2025** to ensure all states frame their respective rules.
 
• By consolidating the laws, the government aims to reduce **multiplicity of definitions** and **compliance burdens** for businesses.
 
• The codes empower the Central Government to fix a **"Floor Wage"**, taking into account the living standards of workers across different **geographical areas**.
 
• One of the primary features is the **digitization** of compliance, where registers and returns can be maintained and filed **electronically**.

questions.question: When is Hindi Journalism Day celebrated every year in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30 May**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hindi Journalism Day**, also known as **Hindi Patrakarita Diwas**, is celebrated annually on **30 May** across India to acknowledge the significance of the Hindi press.
 
• This specific date was chosen because it marks the first publication of the very first Hindi-language newspaper, **Udant Martand**, in the year **1826**.
 
• The newspaper was established and edited by **Pt. Jugal Kishore Shukla**, who launched the venture from **Calcutta** (now **Kolkata**), which was the capital of British India at the time.
 
• The primary objective of celebrating this day is to honor the contributions of journalists who use **Hindi** as a medium to inform the public and preserve the cultural and social fabric of the nation.
 
• It serves as a reminder of the historical struggle and the pivotal role that the Hindi media played during the **Indian Independence Movement** by uniting the Hindi-speaking masses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Udant Martand:**
 
 
• The name of the newspaper, **Udant Martand**, literally translates to "**The Rising Sun**."
 
• It was a **weekly** newspaper published every **Tuesday**.
 
• **Pt. Jugal Kishore Shukla**, its founder, was a lawyer originally from **Kanpur**, **Uttar Pradesh**, who moved to **Calcutta** to start this historic initiative.
 
• Despite its groundbreaking nature, the newspaper faced severe financial challenges due to high **postal rates** and a lack of government patronage, leading to its closure on **December 11, 1827**.
 
 
 
• **Early Indian Press:**
 
 
• The first-ever newspaper published in India was the **Bengal Gazette** (also known as **Hicky's Bengal Gazette**), started by **James Augustus Hicky** in **1780**.
 
• Before the rise of the Hindi press, newspapers in India were primarily published in **English**, **Bengali**, and **Persian**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **First Hindi Daily:** While **Udant Martand** was the first weekly, the credit for the first **Hindi daily** newspaper goes to **Samachar Sudhavarshan**, which began publication in **1854** under the editorship of **Shyam Sundar Sen**.
 
• **Regional Expansion:** The **Banaras Akhbar**, published in **1844** by **Raja Shiv Prasad ‘Sitare-Hind’**, is considered the first Hindi newspaper issued from a **Hindi-speaking region**.
 
• **Related Observances:**
